source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

24025.t:
Harford County stayed Republican in the race for governor, but by a slightly smaller margin than in 2024. Cox beat Moore here 58,978 to 46,383, about 11 points, after Trump carried the county by about 14. That is a move of 2 points toward the Democrats, almost exactly the typical move among Maryland's 24 counties. It is half of Moore's 4-point gain statewide and far smaller than the typical 14-point shift nationally. Nearby comparisons were mixed: Calvert and St. Mary's moved about 3 points left, and Dorchester moved 3 points right.

Turnout fell to 109,907 votes, 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

24037.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, St. Mary's County stayed Republican but by less than in 2024. Cox carried it over Moore by 13 points, 22,923 votes to 17,412, after Trump won it by 17. That is a 4-point move toward the Democrats, slightly less than the state's 5-point shift but more than the typical Maryland county's 3. It ranks 9th of 24 counties by move.

Turnout was 72% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among comparable counties, Calvert moved 3 points left, Washington 10, and Somerset moved 1 point right. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points toward the Democrats, far more than St. Mary's.

24017.t:
In the race for governor, Charles County gave Moore 50,448 votes to Cox's 16,232, a Democratic margin of 49 points. That is 9 points more Democratic than Harris's 41-point margin here in 2024. It is a bigger swing than Maryland's 5-point shift and the fifth-largest of the state's 24 counties. Similar Maryland counties moved left by 5 points (Howard), 10 (Montgomery) and 3 (Baltimore). Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout fell sharply: 69,528 votes were cast, 76% of the 91,650 in 2024. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

24011.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Caroline County moved slightly against the statewide tide. Republican Cox carried it 7,759 to 3,319 over Democrat Moore, a margin of about 39 points, compared with Trump's 38-point win here in 2024. That is a shift of less than a point toward the Republicans, while Maryland as a whole moved about 3 points toward the Democrats and the typical county nationally moved 14 points left.

Turnout fell to 11,525 votes, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar Maryland counties, Queen Anne's moved by the same small amount toward the Republicans, Cecil edged a point left, and Allegany moved about 7 points left.

24015.t:
In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, Cecil County stayed firmly Republican but moved about 4 points toward the Democrats, from Trump's 31-point margin in 2024 to Cox's 27-point lead, 20,717 votes to 11,531. That is close to the typical Maryland county's 3-point shift and smaller than the state's 5-point move. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points left.

Only 33,569 votes were cast, about 64% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move. Among similar counties, Queen Anne's and Carroll barely moved, while Washington shifted 10 points toward the Democrats.

24041.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Talbot County moved about 2 points toward the Republicans. It was an exact tie between Harris and Trump in 2024; this time Cox beat Moore 9,052 to 8,776, a margin of about 2 points. Turnout was 81% of the 2024 vote, with 18,326 ballots against 22,667, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

Talbot ran against the tide. Maryland moved 4 points left as Moore won statewide, and 18 of 24 counties moved left. Talbot ranked 22nd. Kent, a similar county, moved about 3 points right. Wicomico and Calvert moved 2 and 3 points left. Nationally, the typical county shifted 14 points toward the Democrats.

24013.t:
In the race for governor, Carroll County barely budged. Cox, the Republican, carried it 44,749 to 26,386 over Moore, a 25-point margin, essentially the same as Trump's 25-point win here in 2024. The county moved less than a point toward the Democrats, against a typical 3-point shift among Maryland counties and 5 points statewide. It ranked 19th of 24 in the state by move. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Carroll cast 74,114 votes, 73% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among comparable Maryland counties, Queen Anne's and Worcester were also nearly flat, while Washington moved 10 points toward the Democrats.

24023.t:
In the governor's race, Dan Cox carried Garrett County over Wes Moore by 7,909 votes to 2,432, a margin of 51 points. That is 3 points narrower than Donald Trump's 54-point win over Kamala Harris here in 2024, the same shift toward the Democrats as Maryland as a whole. The move ranks ninth among the state's 24 counties, where the typical county shifted 1 point left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Only 10,671 votes were cast, 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Allegany moved 7 points left, Cecil 1 point left and Caroline 1 point right.

24005.t:
In the governor's race, Baltimore County backed Moore over Cox by 28 points, 183,982 votes to 101,738, up from Harris's 25-point margin over Trump in 2024. That 3-point move toward the Democrats is smaller than the statewide shift of 5 points and close to the typical Maryland county's 3, placing it 13th of 24 in the state. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left. Among similar counties, Anne Arundel moved 4 points, Howard 5 and Frederick 10.

The county cast 299,518 votes, the second-most in Maryland but only 73% of its 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

24035.t:
Queen Anne's County barely moved in the race for governor. Cox, the Republican, carried it by 28 points, 15,291 votes to 8,503 for Moore, almost exactly matching Trump's 28-point margin in 2024. That is a shift of less than half a point toward the Democrats, while Maryland as a whole moved 5 points left and the typical county in the state moved 3. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout fell to 24,682 votes, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Comparable counties were similarly steady: Carroll was flat, Worcester moved 1 point right, and Cecil moved 4 points left.

24009.t:
Calvert County stayed Republican in the race for governor but by a smaller margin. Cox beat Moore 20,696 to 17,370, a margin of about 8 points, down from Trump's 11-point win here in 2024. That 3-point move toward the Democrats is a little smaller than Maryland's 4-point shift and close to the typical Maryland county's 2 points. It also sits alongside the similar counties of St. Mary's, Wicomico and Harford, each of which moved 2 to 3 points. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

About 39,693 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell whether people changed their minds or some simply stayed home.

24047.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Cox beat Moore in Worcester County 14,286 votes to 8,842, a margin of 23 points. That is about one point more Republican than Trump's 22-point win here in 2024, while Moore carried the state by 33 points, four more than Harris did. Worcester ranks 19th of Maryland's 24 counties by move. Eighteen counties moved left, the typical one by 2 points, and nationally the typical county moved 14 points left. Among similar counties, Queen Anne's barely moved, while Washington shifted 9 points left and St. Mary's 3.

Only 23,965 votes were cast, 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 94% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24043.t:
Washington County stayed Republican in the race for Maryland governor but by a much smaller margin. Cox beat Moore here 27,383 to 20,779, a margin of 13 points, compared with Trump's 23-point win in 2024. That 10-point shift toward the Democrats is the third-largest among Maryland's 24 counties and about twice the statewide move of 5 points. Nearby comparisons barely shifted: Carroll was flat, Worcester moved slightly right, and St. Mary's moved 4 points left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout fell sharply. The county cast 50,191 votes, 69% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters staying home.

24033.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Prince George's County gave Moore 228,680 votes to Cox's 18,007, a Democratic margin of 82 points. That is 7 points more Democratic than the county's 75-point margin for Harris over Trump in 2024, more than double the state's 3-point shift and well above the typical Maryland county's 1-point move. It ranks fifth of 24 counties by shift. Nearby comparisons varied: Montgomery moved 10 points, Howard 5 and Baltimore 1.

Only 256,249 votes have been counted, 64% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 79% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

24019.t:
In the governor's race, Dorchester County moved about 3 points toward the Republicans, the largest rightward shift among Maryland's 24 counties. Cox beat Moore here by about 18 points, 7,274 votes to 4,991, compared with Trump's roughly 15-point win over Harris in 2024. Statewide, Moore won by 33 points, a 4-point gain on the 2024 presidential result, and 18 of Maryland's counties moved left.

Dorchester cast 12,790 votes, 76% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Somerset moved 1 point right, while St. Mary's and Calvert each moved about 3 points left. Nationally, 2,679 of 2,775 counted counties moved left.

24031.t:
In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, Montgomery County gave Moore 262,549 votes to 55,992, a margin of D+63. That is 10 points more Democratic than Harris's D+53 in 2024, the largest move of Maryland's 24 counties, where the typical county moved about 1 point and the state moved 3. It also outpaced similar neighbors Prince George's (+7), Charles (+8) and Howard (+5), though it trailed the national typical move of 14 points.

Only 328,738 votes are in, 64% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With about 79% of the expected vote counted, these numbers may still move.

24045.t:
In the race for governor between Moore and Cox, Wicomico County stayed Republican but by less than it voted for Trump in 2024. Trump carried it by about 6 points; Cox leads by about 1, with 16,160 votes to Moore's 15,775. That is a 4-point move toward the Democrats, slightly less than Maryland's 5-point statewide shift but more than the typical county in the state (3 points), and well below the 14-point typical move nationally. Similar counties went both ways: Calvert moved 3 points left, while Talbot and Kent moved 1 and 3 points right.

Turnout was 71% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 94.9% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24001.t:
In the governor's race, Allegany County voted for Cox over Moore by 31 points, 13,859 votes to 7,139. That is 10 points closer than Trump's 40-point win over Harris in 2024. It was the fourth-largest move toward the Democrats among Maryland's 24 counties, where the typical county moved 3 points left and the state as a whole moved 5. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Allegany cast 21,861 votes, 68% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar Republican-leaning counties moved less: Caroline barely shifted, Queen Anne's moved less than a point, and Cecil moved 4.

24003.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Anne Arundel County voted for Moore over Cox by 18 points, 131,776 to 90,440, up from Harris's 14-point margin in 2024. That 4-point shift toward the Democrats is close to the typical Maryland county's move of 3 points and a little smaller than the state's 5-point shift, as Moore won statewide by 34. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left. Turnout was 75% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Among similar Maryland counties, Frederick moved 10 points toward the Democrats, Baltimore County moved 3, and Talbot moved about a point toward the Republicans.

24029.t:
In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, Kent County moved about 4 points toward the Republicans, from a 3-point Trump margin in 2024 to a 6-point Cox lead, 4,214 votes to 3,698. Statewide, Moore won by 32 points, 3 better than Harris. Kent ranks 22nd of Maryland's 24 counties by move, while nationally 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moved left. Similar counties split: Talbot and Dorchester also moved right, by 2 and 5 points, while Wicomico moved 2 points left.

The 8,193 votes counted so far are 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 90% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

24039.t:
Somerset County, Maryland's smallest by votes cast, edged slightly toward the Republicans in the governor's race. Cox beat Moore here 4,312 to 2,946, an 18-point margin, compared with Trump's 17-point win in 2024: a shift of about 1 point to the right. Statewide, Moore won by 33 points, a 4-point move left from the 2024 presidential result. Somerset ranked 20th of 24 Maryland counties by move. Eighteen counties moved left, the typical one by 2 points, and nationally the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout was 7,520 votes, 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Nearby comparisons split: Dorchester moved 3 points right, Worcester 1 right and St. Mary's 3 left.

24510.t:
**Note to editor:** FIPS 24510 is Baltimore City, not Baltimore County (24005). A 2024 margin of D+73 also fits the city. Please confirm which one this is before publishing. The note below doesn't name the place, so it works either way.

In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, this jurisdiction went D+74, with 117,404 votes for the Democrat to 13,446 for the Republican. Harris carried it by 73 points in 2024, so the margin moved 1 point toward the Democrats. That is slightly more than the typical Maryland county (+1) but well short of similar places: Prince George's moved 7 points, Montgomery 10 and Howard 5.

Only 71% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. Turnout so far is 61% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

24027.t:
Howard County moved 5 points toward the Democrats in the race for governor. Moore beat Cox here by 47 points, 99,539 votes to 33,909, up from Harris's 42-point margin over Trump in 2024. That shift almost exactly matches the statewide move of 5 points and ranks seventh among Maryland's 24 counties. It is larger than the typical Maryland county's 3 points but well below the typical national move of 14.

Turnout fell to 139,538 votes, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among comparable Democratic counties in the state, Charles moved 9 points and Montgomery 10, while Baltimore County moved 3.

24021.t:
In the race for governor between Moore and Cox, Frederick County went for Moore by 19 points, 66,338 votes to 44,608. In 2024 Harris carried it by 9, so the county moved 10 points toward the Democrats. That is the second-largest shift among Maryland's 24 counties, where the typical county moved 3 points and the state as a whole moved 5. It is smaller than the typical move nationally of 14 points. Anne Arundel, a comparable county that started out more Democratic, moved 4 points.

Turnout fell sharply: 115,276 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total. The count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.
